items.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: My first was with Gil Evans in ’76

ctx.x: Because it’s an interesting story. I was, for many years I took great pleasure when people would say, because I’d been working hard to try and do the bass thing and people would say, “Wow Bob, sounds great, it sounds just like a bass.” I’d get all proud and just stick my chest out, you know what I mean? Because that’s what I’d been trying to do, just to find the technique of how to make that role and feel like a bass player playing. And so I put a quartet together, Jon Clarke and I, a French horn player. And…
and the feelings of that style of music. So I have, I think one of the tunes on, it’s called “Hambone.” And it has that New Orleans kind of feeling to it.
